findings.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — P1 confidence 100: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);` treats the all-groups VIEW scope as global management authority, so a view-only administrator passes `requireManage()` and can create groups despite lacking MANAGE.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122 — P1 confidence 100: `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` confuse authorization-resource IDs with GroupModel IDs, so per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants neither resolve the named group resource nor constrain user searches to the granted groups, making member visibility fail while an all-groups fallback can be evaluated against the wrong resource.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121 — P2 confidence 100 advisory: `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> {` performs an unbounded full scan and permission evaluation for every group resource on each user search/count request, so realms with many group grants incur O(groups) authorization work before the user query; although the author can argue filtering must discover all grants, a maintained subject-to-group grant index or batched authorization lookup deletes the per-request scan and its one-evaluation-per-group fan-out.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — P1, confidence 100: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);` makes an all-groups VIEW grant satisfy `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()`'s `requireManage()` check, so a read-only administrator can create or move top-level groups, and the new coverage never verifies that VIEW remains non-mutating.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122 — P1, confidence 100: `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW_MEMBERS, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_MEMBERS)` passes the authorization resource's internal ID to a lookup by resource name and therefore drops every resource-specific group grant, making user count/search requests return successful empty or truncated results for admins whose visible users come from `view-members` or `manage-members`.

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/ModelToRepresentation.java:176 — P2, confidence 75: deleting `public static Stream<GroupModel> searchGroupModelsByAttributes(KeycloakSession session, RealmModel realm, Map<String,String> attributes, Integer first, Integer max)` is unrelated to adding the Groups authorization resource and breaks source/binary compatibility for extensions compiled against this public server-private SPI helper.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — P1, confidence 100: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);` makes an all-groups `view` grant satisfy `canManage()`, so `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` authorizes a read-only administrator to create or reparent arbitrary realm groups.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java:82 — P2, confidence 75: the new group-derived role-mapping branch `return hasPermission(user, null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES) || canManageByGroup(user);` is never exercised by `testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers`, which only updates the user, so a regression that denies role mapping under `MANAGE_MEMBERS` passes this suite.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java:91 — P2, confidence 75: the new group-derived membership branch `return hasPermission(user, null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP) || canManageByGroup(user);` is never exercised with `MANAGE_MEMBERS`, so a regression that denies membership changes to group managers passes this suite.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:306 — P2, confidence 100: `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).users().get(bobId).joinGroup(topGroup.getId());` asserts only that no exception is thrown and never reads Bob's groups, so an endpoint that returns success without persisting membership makes `testManageGroupMembership` pass falsely.

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121 — P2 confidence 100 advisory: `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> {` performs an unbounded full scan and permission evaluation for every group resource on each user search/count request, so realms with many group grants incur O(groups) authorization work before the user query; although the author can argue filtering must discover all grants, a maintained subject-to-group grant index or batched authorization lookup deletes the per-request scan and its one-evaluation-per-group fan-out.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code at line 121 calls resourceStore.findByType() which iterates over all group resources and performs hasPermission() evaluation for each one. This is a valid performance concern for realms with many groups. However, this is not a bug - the code functions correctly. It's an architectural/performance concern about the new V2 implementation. The finding is grounded in actual diff code and raises a legitimate scalability issue, though it's advisory rather than a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — P1, confidence 100: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);` makes an all-groups VIEW grant satisfy `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()`'s `requireManage()` check, so a read-only administrator can create or move top-level groups, and the new coverage never verifies that VIEW remains non-mutating.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java line 70, the canManage() method returns true if hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) - meaning VIEW scope satisfies the manage check. This is inconsistent with the documented behavior in GroupPermissionEvaluator.java which states canManage() should return true for MANAGE permission, not VIEW. In GroupsResource.java, addTopLevelGroup() calls auth.groups().requireManage() which uses canManage(). With this implementation, a user with only VIEW permission on groups would pass the requireManage() check and be able to create top-level groups, which is a privilege escalation bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122 — P1, confidence 100: `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW_MEMBERS, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_MEMBERS)` passes the authorization resource's internal ID to a lookup by resource name and therefore drops every resource-specific group grant, making user count/search requests return successful empty or truncated results for admins whose visible users come from `view-members` or `manage-members`.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in GroupPermissionsV2.java lines 115-125, the getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() method iterates over resources and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...). However, examining the hasPermission() method at lines 131-157, when groupId is not null, it does: resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). The issue is that groupResource.getId() returns the internal resource ID, but findByName() expects the resource name (which based on the schema would be the group's actual ID, not the authorization resource's internal ID). This mismatch means the lookup will fail to find the resource, causing the permission check to fall back to the type-level resource check, which may not grant the same permissions. This would result in group-specific VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants being ignored, leading to truncated or empty user search results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/ModelToRepresentation.java:176 — P2, confidence 75: deleting `public static Stream<GroupModel> searchGroupModelsByAttributes(KeycloakSession session, RealmModel realm, Map<String,String> attributes, Integer first, Integer max)` is unrelated to adding the Groups authorization resource and breaks source/binary compatibility for extensions compiled against this public server-private SPI helper.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows removal of the public static method `searchGroupModelsByAttributes` from ModelToRepresentation.java (lines 176-178 removed). This method was part of the server-spi-private module which is a semi-public API that extensions may depend on. The finding correctly identifies that this deletion could break binary/source compatibility for any extensions that were calling this method. The single call site in GroupsResource.java was updated to call `session.groups().searchGroupsByAttributes()` directly instead. While this is a valid API cleanup, removing public methods from SPI modules without deprecation is a legitimate compatibility concern, though server-spi-private has weaker compatibility guarantees than server-spi.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — P1, confidence 100: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);` makes an all-groups `view` grant satisfy `canManage()`, so `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` authorizes a read-only administrator to create or reparent arbitrary realm groups.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() at line 70, it returns true if hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) - meaning either VIEW or MANAGE scope grants canManage(). This is incorrect because VIEW permission should not grant management capabilities. In GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup(), the code calls auth.groups().requireManage() which checks canManage(). With this bug, a user with only VIEW permission on all-groups would pass the canManage() check and be able to create top-level groups. Comparing to canView() which correctly uses VIEW and MANAGE scopes (read operations), canManage() should only check for MANAGE scope, not VIEW.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java:82 — P2, confidence 75: the new group-derived role-mapping branch `return hasPermission(user, null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES) || canManageByGroup(user);` is never exercised by `testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers`, which only updates the user, so a regression that denies role mapping under `MANAGE_MEMBERS` passes this suite.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new `canMapRoles` method in UserPermissionsV2.java (lines 78-82) includes logic for `MAP_ROLES` permission and `canManageByGroup(user)`, but the test `testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers` only tests user update operations (via `update()` method), not role mapping operations. The test creates a `MANAGE_MEMBERS` permission and verifies the user can be viewed and updated, but doesn't test the role mapping path. This is a valid observation about missing test coverage for the new role-mapping permission logic, though the finding slightly overstates it - the code path for `canManageByGroup` IS tested (just not specifically for role mapping scenarios).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java:91 — P2, confidence 75: the new group-derived membership branch `return hasPermission(user, null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP) || canManageByGroup(user);` is never exercised with `MANAGE_MEMBERS`, so a regression that denies membership changes to group managers passes this suite.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misunderstands the code. The `canManageGroupMembership` method in UserPermissionsV2.java checks if a user can manage their own group membership (i.e., which groups they belong to), not whether someone can manage members of a group. The `canManageByGroup(user)` call delegates to `root.groups()::canManageMembers` which in GroupPermissionsV2.java does check for `MANAGE_MEMBERS` scope. The test suite in GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java includes `testManageGroupMembership()` which tests the `MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP` scope on groups combined with `MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP` on users. The claim that MANAGE_MEMBERS is never exercised is incorrect - it's checked via the canManageByGroup delegation chain.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:306 — P2, confidence 100: `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).users().get(bobId).joinGroup(topGroup.getId());` asserts only that no exception is thrown and never reads Bob's groups, so an endpoint that returns success without persisting membership makes `testManageGroupMembership` pass falsely.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test `testManageGroupMembership` only verifies that `joinGroup()` doesn't throw an exception, without asserting that the user was actually added to the group. Looking at the diff, the test at line 306 calls `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).users().get(bobId).joinGroup(topGroup.getId());` but never verifies the membership was persisted (e.g., by checking `getGroups()` on the user). This is a legitimate test quality concern - the test could pass even if the endpoint silently fails to persist. However, this is a test completeness issue rather than a bug in the production code.
